title: Part Three, Chapter 3: The Wives and the Peoples

verses.t: And then their wives were given to them; and likewise, by a miracle, they took counsel again, and while the men were sleeping they carried out the plan. And a beautiful woman was with Balam-quitzé, another with Balam-acab, another with Mahucutah and another with Yquibalam; and they already had their wives when they woke from sleep, and then they rejoiced in their wives. And these were the names of their wives: Caha-paluma, the wife of Balam-quitzé; Chomiha, the wife of Balam-acab; Tzununiha, the wife of Mahucutah; and Caquixaha, the wife of Yquibalam. And these were the names of their wives, who were made ladies; and these were the ones who multiplied all the peoples, small and great, and these are the origin of us, the Quichés. And the mighty were very many, and they were not only four; yet only four were the fathers of us, the Quichés. And each one's names were different when they multiplied there in the East, and the names of the people were many: some were called Tepeu, others Oloman, Cohah, Quenech, Ahan. So they were called there in the East, where they multiplied; and the origin of the people of Tanub and of Ylocab is also known. They came together from there in the East. Balam-quitzé is the father of the nine great houses of Caviquib; Balam-acab is the father of the nine great houses of Nihaibab; Mahucutah is the father of the four great houses of Ahan-Quiché. There were thirteen families, and the name of their grandmother and father, from whom they multiplied there in the East, was not lost. And likewise came Tanub and Ylocab with the thirteen families that were branches of peoples, and thirteen families with those of Rabinal, the Cakchiquels, those of Ahquiquinaha, and also with those of Sacahib, and with those of Maquib, Cumatz, Cuhalha, Vchabaha, Ahchamilaha, with those of Aquibaha, and Abatenaba, Aculvinac, Balamiha, Cancha-heleb and Balam-colob. And these alone were the chief branches of the peoples, as we call them; we have mentioned only the chief ones. And many were those who came out with each of the families, whose names we do not write, and who multiplied there in the East; and many were those who multiplied while it was still dark, before the sun shone and there was light. And they were all together, and many were the things they did there in the East; and they had not enough to eat, but raised their faces to the sky and did not know how to go far away. And there in that sweetness were white men and black men, and there were many tongues, and men of two ears; and there are different races in the world, and there are homelands of some men whose faces have not been seen, who have no houses but wander like madmen over all the hills. This they said, scorning the homelands of others, they said, there where they saw the East. And at that time they did not worship idols, but were all of one tongue, and kept only the command of the Creator, the Heart of the Sky and of the Earth. And they only waited for the sun to rise; and the great ones and the lords spent their time only in praying, raising their faces to the sky, when they asked for sons and daughters, and they said: "Oh you, Creator and Former, look upon us, hear us; do not leave us, do not forsake us, you god, sky and earth, Heart of the Sky and of the Earth. Give us our descendants for ever, when it dawns, and give us many good and broad roads, and give us peace, a quiet, calm and good life, and customs and being; you, Huracán, Chipi-caculha, Raxa-caculha, Chipi-nanavac, Raxa-nanavac, Voc, Hun-ahpu, Tepeu, Cucumatz, Alomga-holom, Xpiyacoc, Xmucane, grandmother of the sun, grandmother of the light, when it dawns and grows bright." This is what they said as they greeted and invoked and awaited the rising of the sun; and likewise they watched the place where the sun rises, and they watched the morning star, a great star that heralded the rising of the sun, which was to light the whole sky and the earth, by which the creatures would walk.
